before: The limiting size densities differ with spatial dimension: one dimensional length is Rayleigh, two dimensional area is exponential, and three dimensional volume has an integrable divergence at zero. Their survival curves coincide after transformation to U=βs^(2/d), where Pr(U>u)=e^(−u). These are exact calculations from the high-threshold limiting law, not finite-threshold simulations or measured histograms. Based on Mainali et al. (2025), main Eq. 1, p. 1111, and Methods S3.
after: The limiting size densities differ with spatial dimension: one dimensional length is Rayleigh, two dimensional area is exponential, and three dimensional volume has a density that rises without bound as size approaches zero, while its integral remains one. Their survival probabilities, the probabilities of exceeding a threshold, coincide after transformation to $U=\beta s^{2/d}$, where $\Pr(U>u)=e^{-u}$. These are exact calculations from the high-threshold limiting law, not finite-threshold simulations or measured histograms. Based on Mainali et al. (2025), main Eq. 1, p. 1111, and Methods S3.
reason: Explain the needed density/survival meanings directly and render both transformed formulas as math.
meaning_change: No intended change. Focused truth recheck should confirm normalized integrability, limit at zero and Pr(U>u), with the high-threshold-only qualification retained.
